title: 装備移転三原則「非核」の削除案
body:
政府は防衛装備品の輸出ルールを定めた防衛装備移転三原則の前文を改定する検討に入った。核政策の基本方針「非核三原則を守るとの基本原則を堅持してきた」との記述について装備輸出とは直結しないなどとして削除。輸出を前提に装備品の開発や生産を進める考え方を盛り込む方向だ。平和国家の歩みや専守防衛の文言は維持するが、理念変容につながる恐れがある。複数の関係者が17日、明らかにした。【図解】非核三原則を巡る政府の検討状況
装備移転三原則は政府が年末に改定する安全保障関連3文書に含まれない。ただ、3文書でも装備輸出推進の方針を示すため、内容を整合させた上で閣議決定する方針だ。3文書では、非核三原則のうち「持ち込ませず」の例外を明記する案を検討しており、前文の見直しがどう影響するのか注目される。関係者によると、改定案では、非核三原則に関する記述や「他国に脅威を与えるような軍事大国とはならない」との表現を削除。代わりに平和国家としての基本理念や専守防衛、積極的平和主義などに関する姿勢は変わらないと強調する。

title: 経済損失1.2兆円 男性更年期対策
body: 11月19日はジェンダー平等や、男性の心身の健康を考える国際男性デー。女性に比べて、あまり知られていない男性の更年期障害について、国や企業も対策に乗り出している。【写真】娘に声荒らげ、眠れぬ夜…52歳を襲った異変　正体は「男性更年期」経済産業省は、男性の更年期症状による欠勤や離職などの経済損失を年約1.2兆円と試算する。政府は昨年6月の「骨太の方針」で、性差に由来する健康課題に「男性の更年期障害を含む」と初めて明記した。■唾液検査で促す、本人の早い気付き職場で気付く仕組みをつくる企業もある。損害保険ジャパンは2024年度、社員向けのオンライン研修に男性更年期を盛り込んだ。今年度からは、50歳以上のリーダー職らの希望者を対象に、テストステロン値を調べる唾液（だえき）検査も始めた。費用は会社が全額負担し、プライバシーに配慮して、セルフチェックの細かい回答は会社に伝わらない仕組みにした。■「入り口違い」で遠のく適切な治療狙いは、本人に早く気付いてもらうことだ。同社の統括産業医で、診療所長の大村寛敏さんは、唾液検査を「診断ではなく、気付きのためのファーストステップ」と位置づける。大村さんによると、不調を誰にも打ち明けられずに抑うつ的になり、本来は泌尿器科にかかるべきところを、心療内科などを受診する人も少なくないという。「入り口が違うと全く違う方向に行ってしまい、本人が自分を責めることにもなりかねない」今後は新任リーダー向けの研修でも取り上げ、部下や同僚の不調に気付き、ケアできるようにするという。人事部健康経営推進グループの岩堀真駒さんは「『この症状は、もしかしたら男性更年期かもしれない。セルフチェックをやってみたら？』。職場でそんな言葉が飛び交うようになってほしい」と話す。（比嘉太一）

title: 東京・新橋の駅前ビルから出火
body: 東京消防庁によりますと、きょう午前10時50分ごろ港区新橋の「新橋駅前ビル1号館」で「ビルが燃えて煙がすごい」と119番通報がありました。【写真で見る】周囲は騒然…東京･新橋駅前のビルで火災　現場の様子警視庁によりますと、1階の飲食店で調理中に火が出たとみられるということです。店の壁が燃えていて、消防車など21台が出動し消火にあたっていますが、現在のところ、けが人や逃げ遅れた人はいないということです。

title: NHK 職員に「飲み会22時頃まで」
body:
飲酒に絡んだトラブルが相次ぎ対策を検討しているNHKが、飲酒を伴う会食を原則午後10時ごろまでとし、約3時間以内に収めるなど「節度ある飲酒のあり方」を求める通達を職員に出したことが17日、関係者への取材で分かった。【詳報】NHK職員が出演者から性被害　復職後も3年間異動かなわず
関係者によると、通達は17日付。時間はあくまで目安で、時間を超過しても処分などの対象にはしない。NHK関係者は取材に、通達を出すことで不要な会食を抑制し、誘われた際に断りやすくする効果を期待していると説明した。NHKは8月、職員が懇親会後に番組出演者から性被害に遭ったと発表。9月には、飲酒した上で同意なく性的な身体接触をしたとして、記者を懲戒免職にした。井上樹彦会長は同月の会見で「飲酒に関わるリスク事案が後を絶たず、軽視できない」として、対策の検討を関係部局に指示したと明らかにしていた。

title: 市が誤送付した個人情報 SNS拡散
body: 長崎市が児童扶養手当の通知書を同姓同名の別人に誤って送付し、その書類を受け取った人物が、本来の宛先である人物の「住所」などが写った状態の書類画像をSNSに無断投稿していたことが分かりました。▶▶【実際の投稿画像を見る】「名前あってんのに住所違うよ。間違いかな?」…住所消さず■同姓同名に誤送付…届いた人物から指摘誤送付されたのは、主に「ひとり親家庭」や親に重度の障害がある家庭などに対し自治体から支給される「児童扶養手当」の通知書です。長崎市によりますと、10月28日に対象者約3千件に発送したうちの一通を、同姓同名の別人に誤って送っていたということです。■理由は「手作業による封入ミス」長崎市は誤送付が起きた理由について、対象者の中に同姓同名の人物がおり、封筒に書類を手作業で入れていく過程で間違いが起こった「人的ミス」と説明しています。11月2日（月）に、誤って書類が届いた人物から市へ電話連絡があり発覚しました。市は「現時点で他に問い合わせがないため、誤送付は今回の1件のみと考えている」としており、今後確実なチェック体制を徹底し再発防止につとめるとしています。■届いた人物がまさかの「SNS」投稿…住所や番号もこの事態は、単なる行政の事務ミスでは終わりませんでした。本来の受け取り人である被害者によりますと、誤って書類を受け取った人物が、画像から住所や証書番号を消さずにそのままSNS（Threads）に投稿。この投稿が9万回以上表示され、個人情報が拡散する被害へと発展しました。投稿されたのは10月30日で、11月2日になって長崎市の関係者が偶然気づき削除を要請しました。投稿は同日中に削除されましたが、家族構成や経済状況などの極めてプライバシー性の高い情報が、公的機関の事務ミスをきっかけに4日間にわたってネット上に晒される事態となりました。被害女性は行政のミスに憤りを示した上で「ネットリテラシーがなさすぎる…。同じような被害を防ぐため注意喚起と再発防止を求めたい」としています。

title: APECきょう開幕 付近は厳戒態勢
body: きょう、APEC首脳会議が中国で開幕します。史上初の米中ロ首脳会談も開かれる予定で、会場がある広東省深センでは厳戒態勢が敷かれています。【写真で見る】盾を持った警察官も…厳戒態勢の中国･深センの様子記者「会場周辺には多くの警察官が配備されています。この先、会場につながる道はすでに通行止めになっています」APEC首脳会議の会場となる深センでは、厳重な警備態勢が敷かれています。深センはハイテク産業が盛んで、ドローンによる無人配達のサービスが行われていますが、11日から飛行が禁止されています。こうしたなか、きょう未明、ロシアのプーチン大統領が深センに到着しました。空港では中国共産党序列5位の蔡奇・政治局常務委員が出迎えたということです。きょう午後にはアメリカのトランプ大統領や高市総理も到着する予定です。今夜は晩さん会が行われ、あすはトランプ氏と中国の習近平国家主席、ロシアのプーチン大統領による首脳会談が開かれる予定で、3か国による会談は史上初で、首脳らがどのような議論を交わすのか注目されます。

title: 日米豪印が共同文書 中国念頭
body: 日米豪印の4カ国による協力枠組み「クアッド」の首脳会議が17日、フィリピンの首都マニラで開かれた。重要鉱物などで中国への依存を減らすため、供給網（サプライチェーン）強化で協力することで一致。中国を念頭に、輸出規制などによる経済的威圧に深刻な懸念を示す共同文書も発表した。【図解】世界情勢が一目でわかる　米中の「敵」と「味方」2021年に始まった首脳会議は対面では5回目で、24年9月に米国で開催して以来、約2年ぶり。高市早苗首相とトランプ米大統領は初めて参加。インドのモディ首相、オーストラリアのアルバニージー首相も参加した。関税措置などを巡る米印関係の悪化で開催が延期されてきた。19日に中国・深圳で開かれる史上初の米中露首脳会談を前に、日本にとっては自由や民主主義などの基本的価値観を共有する同盟・同志国との結束を示す狙いがある。共同文書では、相次ぐサイバー攻撃を踏まえ、サイバーセキュリティー対策の協力強化を明記。インド太平洋地域の通信インフラを強化するため、電力ケーブルなどエネルギー安全保障面の対策でも連携する。日本主導の外交構想「自由で開かれたインド太平洋（FOIP）」の重要性を強調。安倍晋三元首相によるFOIP提唱から10年となることにも言及した。力や威圧による一方的な現状変更の試みに強く反対する姿勢も示した。インド太平洋地域での海洋監視協力を強化するため、27年にP8、P3C各哨戒機による初の共同飛行訓練を実施する。4カ国の「ビジネスリーダーズ・フォーラム」の初会合を27年の早期に開くことでも一致。地域で信頼できる人工知能（AI）の普及などを支援する重要性も確認した。高市氏ら4カ国首脳は会議で、中国が海洋進出を強める東シナ海・南シナ海を含むインド太平洋地域の情勢について戦略的認識をすり合わせた。イランを含む中東情勢についても議論し、事態の早期沈静化に向けた連携継続を確認した。高市氏は、悪意あるサイバー活動への対処の重要性を強調するとともに、北朝鮮による拉致問題の即時解決に向けた米豪印の支持に謝意を表明した。【マニラ野間口陽】

title: 米大統領 冗談交じりに高市氏評す
body: トランプ米大統領は17日、日米豪印の協力枠組み「クアッド」の首脳会議の記念撮影に応じた際、インドのモディ首相について「彼はタフだ」と述べた後、高市早苗首相について「彼女はもっとタフかもしれない」と冗談交じりに評した。さらに自身とオーストラリアのアルバニージー首相については「私たちは、まあまあだ」とジョークを飛ばした。【図解】世界情勢が一目でわかる　米中の「敵」と「味方」トランプ氏は17日にフィリピンに到着した直後、クアッド首脳会議に臨んだ。「3人や3カ国（日豪印）とはすばらしい関係を築いている」と述べ、友好関係をアピールした。写真撮影開始後、短時間で報道陣は退室を促されたが、トランプ氏は構わずに記者から飛んだ質問に応答した。モディ氏が切り上げるよう促す場面もあった。結局、高市、モディ、アルバニージー各氏は、トランプ氏の独り舞台が続く様子を眺めながら、約4分間立ち続けた。

title: 中国首相 高市氏との接触避けたか
body: 高市早苗首相は17日、訪問先のフィリピンで東南アジア諸国連合（ASEAN）プラス3（日中韓）首脳会議に出席した。中国からは張柱・農業農村相が参加し、李強首相は出席を見送った。高市氏との接触を避けたとみられる。日中関係が悪化した昨秋以来、初となる日中首脳の接触はなかった。【写真】「ポケットに両手」中国アジア局長、駐豪大使へ「栄転」か李氏は15日にフィリピンを訪れ、16日中に帰国。高市氏は同日午後にフィリピンに到着したため、顔を合わせることはなかった。一方、会議では高市氏が隣席の張氏に英語であいさつし、握手する場面もあった。高市氏は「金融協力や食料安全保障に加え、災害対応、組織犯罪（対策）といった共通課題での協力には大きな可能性がある」と強調。会議後、海上貿易やエネルギー・食料安保の強化に関する首脳共同声明が発表された。【マニラ野間口陽、深圳・畠山哲郎】

title: ASEAN 米大統領へ「特別待遇」
body: 【マニラ時事】マニラで15～17日に開かれた東南アジア諸国連合（ASEAN）関連首脳会議では、トランプ米大統領に対する「特別待遇」が際立った。【ひと目でわかる】トランプ米大統領の支持率推移議長国フィリピンはアジア離れが懸念される米国をつなぎ留めるため、トランプ氏の出席を強く働き掛けたようだ。トランプ氏は17日夕にマニラ入りした。一連の会議の閉幕式後にもかかわらず、ASEAN側はトランプ氏との「特別首脳会議」に加え、もてなすための夕食会を開催。18日にはマルコス比大統領との個別会談も予定される。ASEAN側はトランプ氏に合わせ、当初の会議日程を数日後ろにずらした。18日から中国・深センで開かれるアジア太平洋経済協力会議（APEC）首脳会議にトランプ氏が続けて出席できるようにするためだった。カンボジアは15～16日にプノンペンで国際会議を主催したため、フン・マネット首相がマニラ入りしたのは17日。ASEAN加盟国のカンボジアよりも米大統領の出席を優先する異例の対応となった。一方、フィリピンが南シナ海で領有権を争う中国との交流は控えめだった。中国の李強首相は15日夜にマニラに到着し、16日午前にASEAN首脳との会議に臨んだ後、正午すぎにはマニラを離れた。マルコス氏は中国・ASEAN首脳会議に先立ち李氏と言葉を交わす場面はあったが、公式な2国間会談はなかった。ASEAN側がトランプ氏の出席にこだわった背景には、米国のアジア離れへの危機感がある。特に南シナ海で中国と対立するフィリピンにとっては、同盟国でもある米国をアジアに引き留めておく必要がある。トランプ氏は多国間会合を好まないとされ、1期目の2017年にはマニラで米ASEAN首脳会議に出席したが、日程を途中で切り上げ帰国。18～20年は欠席が続いた。トランプ氏は昨年10月にマレーシアで開かれた米ASEAN首脳会議には出席し、「東南アジア諸国と100％共にある」と語った。今回のトランプ氏の訪問は、その言葉を形式上は再確認するものとなった。日本外交筋は「アジア全体にとっていいことだ」と歓迎し、フィリピンの議長国としての成果の一つとの認識を示した。

title: リニア開業時期 年内公表を断念
body: リニア中央新幹線の開業時期について、JR東海は年内の公表を断念しました。ことし7月、JR東海と静岡県が「自然環境保全協定」を結んだことで静岡工区着工の見通しが立ったことを受け、JR東海の丹羽俊介社長が品川・名古屋間の開業時期を「年内に示す」と明らかにしていました。【写真を見る】リニア中央新幹線の開業時期　JR東海は年内発表を断念　静岡工区着工にメドも談合発覚による大成建設への営業停止など響くしかし、工事を請け負う大成建設が談合で営業停止処分を受け、静岡工区の着工が来年春以降にずれ込んだほか、名古屋駅の完成も当初の計画から遅れる見通しとなりました。関係者によりますとこうした状況を踏まえ開業時期の年内公表を断念したということです。18日午後の会見で丹羽社長が説明する見通しです。

title: NVIDIA会長 フアン氏CEO復帰ない
body: [１７日 ロイター] - 米半導体‌大手エヌビデ⁠ィアのハーベイ・​ジョーンズ会長は１７日、取締‌役会としてジ‌ェンスン‌・フアン​氏を最高‌経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）に復‌帰さ​せる意向はな‌いと述べ⁠た。フアン氏は今月、同社⁠の行動規​範や‌基準、企業文化にそぐ⁠わない私⁠的な行動が明⁠らかになったこと‌を受⁠け、自らＣＥＯを​辞任していた。

title: NVIDIA前CEO 復帰なら「光栄」
body: [１７日 ロイター] - 米半導体エヌビディアのジェン‌スン・フアン前最⁠高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１７日、エヌビディア取締役会​が株主と同社にとり最善の利益にな‌ると判断すれば、ＣＥＯに復帰することは「光栄‌だ」と述べた。フ‌アン氏は声明​で「エヌビディアの全員に‌期待されていた基準を満たせな‌かった上、​私生活でも重大な過‌ちを犯した」とし、「取締⁠役会に多大な迷惑をかけ、深く後悔している。私の過⁠ちは全て私の​責任だ」‌と述べた。その上で、自身の辞任後、従業員や投資家、⁠ビジネスパート⁠ナー、顧客から、ＣＥＯとして復帰⁠を望む声が集まっていると説明。‌取⁠締役会の独立調査​に協力していく考えも示した。

title: 個人向け国債 税優遇見送りで調整
body: 政府、与党は2027年度税制改正で、個人向け国債への税制優遇の具体化を見送る方向で調整していることが17日、分かった。相続税を減免したり、少額投資非課税制度（NISA）の対象に加えたりする案が水面下で浮上。ただ、国債の販売は好調で、中小金融機関から預金流出への懸念も寄せられており、早期実施は適さないとの見方が強まった。自民党の小野寺五典税制調査会長は17日のインタビューで、政府が「貯蓄から投資」への流れを後押ししてきた経緯を踏まえ「従来の方針との整合性が論点になる」と指摘した。政府は5日、税制優遇とは別に、国債の品ぞろえを拡充する方針を打ち出した。償還までの期間が長い「超長期債」などの導入を検討する。

title: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
summary: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
body:
Footage shows Ukrainian missile approach Crimea bridge
Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.
Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort.
The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before".
Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic had partially resumed on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - after they had been closed following Russian strikes overnight.
Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.
While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.
The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014.
The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018.
Putin (centre) personally opened the Crimean Bridge by driving a lorry over it in May 2018
In Ukraine, the much-hated bridge is seen as one of the main symbols of Russia's continuing occupation of Ukrainian lands.
"We're drinking champagne!" Andrii, an engineer who lives in Kyiv, told the BBC.
He said the latest attack would "deal a very heavy blow to the morale of the Russians".
Some Ukrainians are concerned that Putin might now respond by carrying out even more attacks against civilian infrastructure, but Andrii said: "I don't think the Russians can make things much worse; they're already pounding us every single night with everything they've got."
Images show the damage to the Crimean Bridge from the overnight attack
The damage after the overnight attack, involving cruise missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section apparently destroyed.
Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below.
Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective".
He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage".
The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and Russia's transport ministry later said some rail services resumed.
Ukraine's state security service SBUsaid its operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders".
Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch.
The Kremlin said Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China.
Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations".
For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry.
Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday.
Watch: BBC reports from Kyiv bridge hit by Russian attack
In Kyiv, loud explosions were heard just before midnight on Monday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies.
On Tuesday, Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had targeted the Southern Bridge, and another three had been fired on the Northern Bridge.
Some of Kyiv's above-ground metro services were also damaged in the overnight attacks, local officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters.
Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River, connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city.
Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials.
The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear, though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly.
The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired.
However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar.
This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.
There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack.
Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.
In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel.
This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdyansk.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control.
Additional reporting by Jaroslav Lukiv

title: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
summary: One of the key symbols of Russia's occupation of Ukraine has suffered major damage after a seven-stage attack by Kyiv.
body:
Footage shows Ukrainian missile approach Crimea bridge
Stretching across the Kerch Strait in the Black Sea, the Crimean Bridge was always a symbol: for Russia, a prestige project cementing its claim to sovereign Ukrainian territory, and for Ukraine, a hated piece of infrastructure emblematic of Moscow's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula.
A key section of the double-arched, 12-mile-long bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said that the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".
But eight years after its unveiling, the bridge has now become material proof of Kyiv's ability to pierce through Moscow's military defences to hit even its most treasured and protected structures.
The attack on the strategic Crimean Bridge was carried out gradually to cut across several layers of defence, Kyiv confirmed on Tuesday.
For several weeks Ukraine's Security Service and its General Staff gradually destroyed air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets, and other designated targets, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
A significant strike had already been reported on 16 November, when drones hit the bridge at night. Traffic was paused briefly then reinstated, and although the arch over the road section was visibly damaged, the structure remained standing.
But that hit turned out to have been only the penultimate stage of a complex attack.
In the early hours of 17 November, the final strikes dealt a fatal blow to the weakened arch structure.
One verified video - filmed from a camera on board a Ukrainian-made Flamingo missile - shows the weapon approaching the main span of the bridge and heading towards the steel arches, with the footage freezing just before impact.
The Flamingo had potentially been modified to be controlled remotely, which improved its accuracy enough to strike the bridge supports, munitions expert Justin Bronk, from the Royal United Services Institute said.
The missile's "very heavy warhead" made it "more suitable" for attacking the bridge's reinforced concrete spans and supports, Bronk added.
Zelensky later confirmed that several types of missiles and drones had been employed in the attack, which led the massive road arch - weighing thousands of tonnes and measuring about 227m in length - to collapse into the strait.
Daylight images taken from the shores of Crimea to the north show a section about 200m (660ft) long of the tarmac was too dragged below into the sea.
This is clearly critical damage to the crossing. Far from just being a decorative feature of the bridge, the arch played a structural role, transferring loads and supporting the span and helping to ensure the stability of the entire structure.
The parallel arch supporting the railway section has remained standing, although it may also have been damaged. All traffic on the bridge was initially suspended, though trains were later allowed to resume running.
But the damage to the bridge's main span is "catastrophic", Colin Capriani, a structural engineer from Monash University in Melbourne, Australia, told BBC Verify. It was "very hard to envisage" how the bridge could be rebuilt given it is clearly well within range of Ukrainian weaponry, Capriani added.
Major attacks in 2022 and 2023 had already caused serious damage to the road spans of the bridge, but the structure survived.
The difference this time is "the most critical and vulnerable part of the bridge has been hit", said David MacKenzie of engineering consultancy COWI, adding that "although the wreckage of the bridge can be cleared fairly quickly, reinstating full road traffic will take over a year".
Moscow uses Crimea as a military base, with airbases, troop concentrations, training grounds and artillery stockpiles. From there it also carries out strikes on the rest of the country and resupplies its troops in southern Ukraine.
The attack comes after a summer of frequent strikes on Crimea, dictated by Ukraine's stated goal of cutting the peninsula off from Russia. At the time, Kyiv vowed to turn the Crimean Peninsula "into an island".
Now - although it is too early to speak of a complete blockade of Crimea – the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis has increased significantly.
There is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions. However, Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar, which has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.
Moscow can also still utilise the ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited - and anything on the Black Sea has become vulnerable to attack. Resupplying Crimea by sea is risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.
In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge - particularly its enormous arch - may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including the occupied cities of Mariupol and Berdyansk.
Away from the operational value of the damage to the bridge, the symbolic significance remains.
In 2018, Putin triumphantly drove over the bridge representing the unification of Russia and Crimea in a Russian-made truck. That section of the road now lies on the seabed.
Nearly five years since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin continues to wreak destruction on Ukraine's civilian population, but his most prized symbols of power are increasingly threatened by Kyiv's reach.

title: Nvidia says it won't reinstate Huang as firm reports bumper results
summary: The AI chip giant reported strong quarterly earnings on Tuesday after the dramatic exit of Jensen Huang.
body:
Jensen Huang and Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress
Nvidia's quarterly sales doubled to top $100bn for the first time as the company insisted it has no plans to reinstate ousted co-founder Jensen Huang.
In the company's first results sinceHuang's dramatic exit, interim chief executive Colette Kress said it is "business as usual" and told investors: "We've got this."
The company's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier, reaching $115.8bn (£86.9bn), with shares in the company jumping by 4.8% in after-hours trading.
Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said hewould be "honoured" to returnand lead Nvidia, having quit following alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected spy for China.
"The board does not intend to reinstate him," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said during a call on Tuesday with financial analysts.
The company's profits also doubled from a year ago. For the quarter, which covered the three months to 25 October, profit hit $65bn. Its revenue from data centres, a significant part of Nvidia's business, also doubled to $107bn in the same period.
Going forward, the company said its rapid growth is poised to continue, and revenue will rise by another 13% in the next quarter.
Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?
Given the uncertainty surrounding the company after Huang's exit, financial analysts had been unsure that Nvidia would provide any forward-looking guidance.
Daniela Hathorn, a senior analyst for trading platform Capital.com, said Nvidia's results "offer a strong answer to concerns that demand for AI infrastructure is cooling" and temper immediate worries that Huang was irreplaceable as a leader.
"The harder question is whether Nvidia can preserve the strategic advantage Huang helped build," Hathorn added. "His exit is unlikely to change orders already committed, but could matter more when Nvidia makes its next round of decisions on products, partnerships and investment."
Kress seemed eager to stress that Nvidia can continue to not only succeed, but lead the ongoing AI buildout that is happening throughout the technology industry.
"It is business as usual," she said. "Our partners, our suppliers, all of them are 100% behind us."
She added that Nvidia's leadership team has "stood up very strongly over the last week... working seamlessly in all of their departments and projects".
"Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed." Kress said before leaving the analyst call. "We've got this."
The interim CEO also said Nvidia is no longer shipping Hopper data centre semiconductors to China.
The Hopper technology is in Nvidia's advanced H200 processors, which the firm wonapproval to sell in Chinaafter Huang's repeated lobbying efforts in Washington.
They had previously been restricted over concerns that selling them to China would give its industries and military an edge over the US.
Kress did not elaborate on why the shipments had been stopped.
The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal
Jensen Huang says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked him
Despite board chairman Jones saying earlier that the company would not answer analysts' questions about Huang or Nvidia's investigation into his conduct, he did address the search for a permanent replacement.
He said Nvidia is working with an executive search firm and is considering internal and external candidates, but that the company would not rush its selection.
"With the advanced technology and the national security dynamics in the marketplace, our new CEO will have to navigate those waters carefully," Jones said. "The search will be thorough and we want to do it as quickly as possible, but we won't do it before we find the exact right person."
Michael Monaghan from investment firm Founder ETFs is among those who want Huang back in the top job at Nvidia.
The Nvidia investor told the BBC that he is waiting to see the results of a thorough investigation into Huang's actions, instead of relying on "salacious allegations" made in the media.
Nvidia's strong earnings are "from the machine that Jensen built" and a company tends to lose "its shine and vision" after an iconic founder leaves, Monaghan said.

title: Thomas Markle charged over child sex abuse material in Philippines
summary: Markle is being held in custody in the US after one charge and has previously denied all of the allegations.
body:
Thomas Markle has also been charged in the US
Police in the Philippines have charged Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material.
The charges were filed on Monday, Cebu province prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC.
Earlier this month, Markle, 82, was separately arrested and charged in the US with possession of child sexual abuse material. The FBI said agents, after searching storage units Markle rented, seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books, that they allege contained child sex abuse material.
Markle, who is in custody in the US, has previously denied the allegations. The BBC has contacted Markle's attorney for comment.
Elmido told the BBC that Philippine National Police had charged Markle Sr with "two counts of intent to distribute CSAEM [child sexual abuse and exploitation material], and one count of possession of CSAEM material".
Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.
Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.
Earlier this month, Markle Sr was arrested and charged in the US. He had initially been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida, but was taken back into custody last weekafter prosecutors alleged he removed his ankle monitor.
Meghan Markle has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.
In a previously shared statement after the allegations against her father emerged, Meghan wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."
She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

title: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
summary: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.
body:
Masha was in her kitchen when she heard the explosions blast through the city
The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions.
Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted.
Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around.
At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide.
The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours.
Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet.
Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles.
Last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the Russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions.
"It was really scary. We had no idea they'd hit here so much. It's like we're cursed," Masha told me, describing grabbing her child and running into the corridor for protection.
But somehow, she still managed to sound cheerful.
"It's difficult, but we're used to it. And we try to take the positive from everything. Like: we survived today! So we can be happy about that."
The Northern Bridge crossing is closed to traffic while emergency response teams work to clear the debris
From the damage, it looks like Russia targeted the same spot on the bridge with a volley of three missiles, aiming to keep the road closed for as long as possible.
A major recovery operation is under way, with firefighters and engineers in fluorescent overalls working to evaluate the extent of the damage. But it looks like the disruption will continue for some time.
Further along the Dnipro River, the Pivdennyi (Southern) bridge was also hit on Monday night, with four missiles.
The metro line across it was suspended for a while, although by mid-afternoon it had been restored. The mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said road transport in one direction was also being partially restored.
On the Pivnichnyi bridge, a man with a bag of tennis rackets on his back was gazing at the crater in front of him. He was heading home from the courts after he had travelled on foot to the left bank.
"It is upsetting," Anatolii told us. "Then when you read the news of what our side did to the Crimea bridge, you do feel a bit better."
The main bridges over the River Dnipro - that cuts through Kyiv - were the target of Russian strikes
That is because there was a battle of the bridges overnight.
Ukrainian missiles hit the one Russia had built to occupied Crimea, and caused serious damage. That bridge is prized by Russian President Vladimir Putin personally, a symbol of his illegal 2014 takeover.
Ukrainians loathe it for the same reason and now a section has collapsed into the sea, along with its towering arch.
To many here, the timing feels significant: a blow to Putin's image, just as he wants to seem most powerful at this week's summit with the US and China.
But for Kyiv resident Antonina, today is just another challenge to overcome.
The 67-year-old, who we met pulling a shopping trolley through the debris on a bridge in the Ukrainian capital, was heading to see her son on the right bank, but taxi drivers were charging a fortune to go round, so she decided to walk.
"What else could I do?" she shrugged.
"It was a very scary night. It felt like something exploded right over my head. We will get through this, but I just wish the war would end."

title: Jeff Bezos says he was 'heavily involved' in casting Robert Pattinson as new 007
summary: The Amazon CEO said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson "because he's already so famous".
body:
Watch: Jeff Bezos on involvement in casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has said he was "heavily involved" in picking actor Robert Pattinson for the role of James Bond in the next 007 film.
Speaking onstage at an event in California, the Amazon CEO said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson - who starred in a number of blockbuster films including Batman and the Twilight franchise - "because he's already so famous".
The role has typically gone to an actor who is not as well-known at the time of casting. But Bezos said in screen tests, "it was so obvious he is James Bond".
This will be the first 007 not under creative control of the Broccoli family, who has overseen the franchise since its start in 1962. Amazon purchased MGM in 2022.
'Good Bond vibes' - Hollywood locals react to Robert Pattinson cast as new 007
"There was something special about Rob", Bezos said at Semafor Silicon Valley & The World Event on Tuesday.
Pattinson was unveiled as the franchise's seventh James Bond on Monday, taking over from actor Daniel Craig. He will star in the 26th Bond movie, due to be released in 2028.
In a statement, the London-born actor said: "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime."
The next Bond film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, but its title and exact release date have not yet been announced.
The announcement comes after years of intense speculation about who will take over from Craig in one of the most high-profile - and highly scrutinised - roles in entertainment.
Several other actors, including Josh O'Connor, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden, were reported to be in the frame for the role as screen tests took place in recent weeks.
But Amazon MGM ultimately went with a household name, choosing a more bankable movie star who is widely seen as a safe pair of hands.
The pick comes amid widespread Hollywood cuts and consolidation, with studios struggling to get people into cinemas.
Hollywood insiders have said Pattinson was viewed as a safe pick to bring audiences in, rather than taking a risk on a new actor who could grow with the franchise.
"Maybe he's boring. Maybe Hollywood would be passing up a chance to anoint a badly needed new star. But with so much at stake for everyone involved, that all makes him the obvious pick," Hollywood journalist Matthew Belloni, who predicted the pick, wrote in his newsletter.
The BBC's Regan Morris contributed to this report.

title: As Trump and Xi meet, China's AI dreams face an unexpected hurdle: the Nvidia spy scandal
summary: China worries the scandal could ramp up pressure on the US  to further restrict the sale of advanced chips.
body:
Jensen Huang is out but his shadow looms over the upcoming meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping this week.
For Beijing, the former Nvidia CEO's dramatic fall is a major challenge - and not just because of claims that a Chinese spy may have honey-trapped Huang, one of the artificial intelligence industry's most influential figures.
Rather, the allegations surrounding Huang and his affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang are turning into a new flashpoint in an already fragile US-China relationship.
US intelligence reports claim she had ties to Beijing's intelligence apparatus - in particular the Ministry of State Security, China's main civilian spy agency.
The claim remains unproven, but it has already reignited debate in Washington over exports of advanced chips to China and whether the Trump administration has been too willing to ease restrictions.
For years now, advanced computer chips have been a key battleground in the US-China rivalry because they are essential for AI, supercomputing and military technology.
Chinese officials are worried this scandal could strengthen voices in Washington who argue in favour of further limiting Chinese access to cutting-edge American tech.
Just this week, the Trump administration introduced new export restrictions on Chinese firms that access advanced US chips in third countries such as Malaysia, Thailand or Brazil. They typically do this by renting computing power in data centres abroad to train their AI models. But some of the firms, like the one Alice Huang worked for, are also accused of smuggling chips to China, although they have denied this.
Until now, this controversy appeared to be a sideshow in US-China relations. But with Beijing calling the new rules "economic coercion" on the eve of Trump arriving in Shenzhen, there is a growing risk it could become something much bigger.
Watch: Jensen Huang speaks to the BBC's Faisal Islam in 2025
Democrats, who will control Congress come January, have made their position clear. Last Wednesday top Democrat Ted Lieu told Politico the Trump administration had been "1,000%" too deferential to Nvidia, putting national security at risk, while fellow Democrat Zoe Lofgren suggested Congress would now be more likely to restrict sales of AI chips to China.
The BBC has approached the White House for comment.
Beijing's foreign ministry had described the spy claims as a "smear against China".
"The US should stop fabricating so-called espionage narratives to find pretexts for imposing technological blockades," spokesperson Mao Ning said last week.
The ministry also seemed keen to keep the meeting on track, saying the two countries had kept "close communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state".
For the last year, Trump and Xi have been seeking to stabilise relations after a damaging tariff war that almost brought trade between the two countries to a standstill.
The Trump administration's decision topermit sales of advanced Nvidia H200 chips to China in late 2025was seen as evidence that both sides were searching for areas of co-operation, even while competition intensified.
It was a rare move given Washington had spent years trying to limit China's access to the most advanced chips.
Many in the US have long viewed these chips as a national security issue, arguing they could strengthen China's military and surveillance capabilities. Jensen Huang, whorejects that claim, advocated lifting bans on the export of high-performing chips to China. Beijing argues the restrictions are an attempt to contain its rise.
Now that opening may be under threat.
History has taught Beijing and Washington that spy scandals rarely remain confined to the intelligence world.
Analysts in China already see echoes of an incident in 2023 when a suspected surveillance balloon drifted through the skies over the US before an American fighter jet shot it down. Beijing insisted it was a civilian meteorological airship that had strayed off course.
The suspected Chinese spy balloon was shot down days after it was spotted over the US
But a planned trip by then US Secretary of State Antony Blinken was cancelled and communication between the two governments deteriorated sharply.
The incident showed how quickly a security dispute could overwhelm diplomatic efforts and push relations into a deep freeze.
"The mere passage of a balloon sent American public opinion and politicians into a state of high alert, as if a "Chinese threat" were looming directly overhead," said the state media outlet, the Global Times this week as it made a direct comparison with the Nvidia scandal.
"No-one on the US side has ever apologised or taken responsibility for the genuine damage this caused to US-China relations," it added.
The state-run outlet also questioned why the Nvidia story had emerged so soon after "the hard-won detente" between Beijing and Washington, following a meeting between the two countries' leaders in September.
"Is someone behind the scenes pushing an agenda and stirring up confrontation?" it asked.
Both Trump and Xi have significant incentives to keep talking.
China's economy remains under pressure and is increasingly reliant on exports. Xi needs trade to keep flowing and this meeting is a key stepping stone to replacing the current trade truce that is due to expire in January.
Meanwhile Trump has repeatedly touted his close relationship with Xi and argued that maintaining dialogue is essential to managing competition between the two powers.
The US president is in his last two years and faces an uphill struggle to pass domestic legislation after the midterms. To counter this, he could be looking for some foreign policy wins.
He may also hope for Xi's help to end the war in the Middle East.
Neither side will want to be discussing intelligence concerns and technology controls instead of trade, investment and economic co-operation.
The summit is also being carefully choreographed by Beijing to show off its technological prowess in Shenzhen - a deeply symbolic choice of city.
It's home to some of the country's biggest tech companies and has become a showcase for Beijing's ambitions in AI and advanced manufacturing.
Also, given Washington's tighter restrictions on advanced chips, Beijing has options for retaliation.
One of its most powerful tools is its dominance of key rare earth minerals. China processes much of the world's supply for materials that are used in everything from electric vehicles and smartphones to military equipment.
Analysts have long warned that technological restrictions can trigger a cycle of retaliation in which each side reaches for its strongest economic leverage.
That would shift the current trend of US-China relations from engagement back towards mutual suspicion.

title: Government backs welfare shake-up to prevent 'lost generation'
summary: Ex-minister Alan Milburn has set out plans to divert spending from benefits towards job support.
body:
The government has backed plans by former minister Alan Milburn for sweeping reforms to prevent "losing a generation" of young people to a life on benefits.
Milburn proposes spending billions on tailored support for under 25s not in employment, education or training (Neets), to be part-funded by cuts to some benefits.
He claims his plan, which also proposes tax breaks for firms and major education reforms, will get 440,000 young people into jobs by 2036.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he endorsed the "principles" of the Milburn review and was confident he could persuade Labour MPs to back legislation to implement its measures.
The PM told Sky News he would set out a full response to the review next month, after he had received a separate report into Personal Independence Payments (Pips) by Social Security Minister Sir Stephen Timms.
But he added: "I have never in my years in politics seen a wholesale, whole government approach to supporting the next generation.
"That is what this represents, and I am absolutely confident that I can take this vision and get people behind it, indeed get the country behind it, because we will not place Britain in the position I want it to be in if we have a generation of young people growing up without hope for the future."
The government has made Milburn the head of a new new youth opportunities unit to deliver on his recommendations.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said her party agreed with Milburn's "diagnosis" but claimed Labour had "made the problem much worse for young people" by increasing employers' National Insurance contributions and the youth minimum wage.
There are few signs so far that Burnham will face a backlash from his own MPs of the scale that blocked his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer's planned £5bn welfare cuts last year.
But some left-wing Labour MPs and the Unison trade union have warned proposals to cut health-related benefits will drive some young people into poverty.
Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden told MPs that "in future" the welfare state should be judged "not just by a snapshot of people's monthly incomes" but "but by the story of people's lives, and by their ability to achieve their full potential".
McFadden, who was flanked by Burnham and Chancellor John Healey during his statement in the Commons, said the government rejected claims that young people were "snowflakes and shirkers".
The million who were not in work or training had been robbed of the "prospect of a good future" and that was something that demanded "much more" than a conventional government response, he told MPs.
He said the government would publish draft proposals on welfare reform early next year, with legislation to follow.
In hiswide-ranging 250 page report,external, Milburn proposes:
An "entirely new benefits system" for under-25s, which would end the health-top up of Universal Credit and Personal Independence Payments (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales
Instead, a new "youth allowance" would be set at the basic rate of Universal Credit for under-25s, with a higher rate for those living independently
A reduction in employers' National Insurance costs for 21- to 24-year-olds, starting in the retail and hospitality sectors, meaning employing those young people would be cheaper
A huge expansion in post-18 college places and a legal right to work, education or training
A new, locally-led Youth Opportunity Service in England to give young people one named advisor and a personalised participation plan
Primary and secondary schools required to identify and support pupils at risk of becoming Neet, and schools obliged to offer work experience
The report calls for the government to spend around £5.8bn in total by 2036-37 on extra mental health and employment support.
And it urges ministers to "kickstart the reform programme" next year, with an initial £500m, from "repriotising" existing spending.
At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report
Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036
Where are the most jobs for 18-24 year-olds?
Milburn has said his plans are not about saving money - and his report says the government will not see overall savings from reduced benefit bills and higher tax receipts until 2036/27, when it will claw back £200m.
But by then, it assumes the share of 16–24-year-olds that are Neet will have gone down from 13% - one of the highest in Europe - to 5%, the lowest in the UK since records began.
Launching his report earlier on Tuesday, Milburn said "half measures will not do" because "the scale of the problem is just too big for that".
He added: "Britain is at risk of losing a generation of young people, not because they lack talent, not because they lack ambition, not because they do not want to work.
"This is not a crisis of aspiration; it is a crisis of opportunity."
Milburn's report has no specific blueprint for Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland, where education, skills, health and local government are devolved.
He said the UK and devolved governments "should agree common definitions, a shared set of headline outcomes and a regular joint review of progress".
Scotland's Education Secretary Màiri McAllan said: "Where there is opportunity to collaborate with the UK government and others for the benefit of young people in Scotland, we will take it."
But she argued many of the reforms recommended for England, such as stronger vocational training, were already in place in Scotland.
A spokesperson for the Welsh government said: "We stand ready to work with the UK government to ensure Wales benefits fully from any UK-wide measures that improve life chances through access to rewarding work."
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said he agreed "with the general drift of the Milburn report, but it's too little and too slow".
"We have a fundamental problem in Britain," he added. "Too many people are being encouraged to go on benefits, and training and apprenticeship schemes that take far too long."
Lib Dem treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said if the government wanted to get people into work, it should back high street firms "that give many their first job", scrap the "unfair jobs tax" and negotiate a new growth and defence partnership with the EU.
Green Party leader Zack Polanski described Milburn's proposals as a "flimsy sticking plaster" that intend to "slash support for disabled young people while subsidising corporations to hire cheap labour".

title: Jensen Huang says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked him
summary: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.
body:
Jensen Huang said he would be "honoured" to return as the boss of tech giant Nvidia if the board asked him to, in his first public comments since his shock resignation.
"I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely," Huang said on X, days after reports he had extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy.
He said he had an "outpouring" of calls from company employees, investors and others calling for him to return as CEO of Nvidia.
But, as theBBC reportedon Monday, Nvidia's board is not considering bringing him back to lead the company.
The prospect of Huang returning at this point looks unlikely.
The company's board isinvestigating his conduct, which includes an alleged affair with an Nvidia executive.
The AI chip giant is set to report its financial results later on Tuesday, during which the company's interim chief executive, Collette Kress, may address the situation with Huang.
Beyond the internal Nvidia investigation, Huang's affair with a woman suspected of being an asset for Beijing is set to see the billionairequestionedbefore multiple committees of US lawmakers in the weeks ahead.
The Nvidia founder said he had "made serious mistakes in my personal life".
Nonetheless, Huang's statement appeared to show some hope he would be able to move past the major corporate scandal.
Huang said people have continued to "reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics".
"If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang added.
Many technology executives in recent days have praised Huang's role in the artificial intelligence boom. A petition began circulating online over the weekend calling for his reinstatement at the company.
Yet, by Monday, many executives were not openly calling for Huang's return.
Brad Gerstner, a major tech investor who knows Huang personally and also holds a significant stake in Nvidia, last week wrote an open letter saying that Nvidia could consider Huang's reinstatement.
On Monday, Gerstner said during an event hosted by Semafor that his letter had been misunderstood and the investigation into Huang's conduct needed to run its course.
While Gerstner questioned the facts around Huang's departure, he added: "I don't know to what degree he misled the board. If I was on a board I would take that very seriously. Let's be clear no one is above the law."

title: At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report
summary: A major review proposes widespread changes to help get young people into work across the UK.
body:
The review has proposed widespread changes to tax, welfare, and education
A major review by former minister Alan Milburn has proposed widespread changes to help get young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) into work across the UK.
His report -which has now been published in full,external- says the UK should aim to reduce the rate of Neet young people from 13% to about 5% by 2036.
Its proposals relate mostly to England, with a recommendation that Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland adapt the principles to suit their own systems.
Here is a summary of the key points from the review:
Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work
Young people should have a legal right to a route into education, training or work, and would be supported to do so under an "opportunity guarantee"
A new, locally-led Youth Opportunity Service in England would give young people one named advisor and a personalised participation plan - spelling out what action needs to be taken, by whom, and when
Tax, spending and other policy decisions should be put through a "youth opportunity test", to ensure they consider impact on younger generations
Prevention should start early, with primary and secondary schools required to identify and support pupils at risk of becoming Neet
Schools would also be required to offer work experience
A new performance measure would assess schools based on where their pupils end up
A new writing, numeracy and oracy check for pupils in Key Stage 3 (Years 7 to 9)
An extra 150,000 18- to 24-year-olds studying further education courses at colleges and other training providers each year
College funding to be based on how students perform and where they end up, rather than on how many students there are
A new digital open college, part-funded by employers and private investors, which would allow young people to study courses from colleges and universities
Aim to double the number of young people completing apprenticeships over the next decade - with more than a third of young people starting one every year
Where has the most jobs for 18-24 year-olds? Use our look-up to find out
Watch: What's in the Milburn review?
The young people caught up in Britain's Neets crisis
An extra 170,000 job and apprenticeship opportunities to be created through employer incentives
Employers who take on any young person who has been Neet for six months should receive a £3,000 payment
Small businesses - with fewer than 50 employees - which do so should receive an extra £2,000
There would be an extra £2,000 payment if the young person has been in care or is disabled
Lower National Insurance costs for 21- to 24-year-olds, starting in retail and hospitality
Large employers should tell job applicants when they are unsuccessful
Young people who are already Neet should have guaranteed access to fast-track services like talking therapies and counselling within three months
These should be accessible without a diagnosis
A new digital-first mental health care service should be the "starting point for young people to access help"
The government should introduce national maximum waiting times for young people's mental health care from 2028
Fitness to work, or "fit notes", to be issued through the new Youth Opportunity Service, rather than GPs
Why Milburn's Neets reforms will only save £200m a year by 2036
An "entirely new benefits system" for under-25s
Young people to no longer get the health top-up of Universal Credit, which provides extra money for people whose health conditions limit their capacity to work
They would also no longer receive Personal Independence Payments (Pip), which help with the extra living costs of having a long-term health condition or disability
Instead, a new youth allowance would be set at the basic rate of Universal Credit for under-25s, with a higher rate for those living independently

An additional cost allowance would replace Pip, providing "targeted financial support where disability-related extra costs are well established, significant and ongoing"
A new severe and complex needs insurance for those who will never be able to work

title: Home secretary plans to tackle 'perception of two-tier policing'
summary: Shabana Mahmood will announce stronger guidance on police impartiality.
body:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is to announce stronger guidance on police impartiality to tackle what she calls the "corrosive and growing perception of two-tier policing".
She will tell a conference of police chiefs that they should avoid what she calls "misguided attempts at course correction" where the pursuit of equality leads instead to differential treatment.
Recent complaints about alleged two-tier policing have mostly come from those on the right in politics.
They have pointed to the arrest of Henry Nowak as he was dying after being stabbed by Vickrum Digwa who had accused him of racism.
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has argued that white people are treated differently by police because of their race. But critics say this claim risks overlooking the long‑standing experiences of black and minority ethnic communities.
Some senior police figures have alsostrongly rejected the claimof two-tier policing.
Mahmood will announce a new national standard is being developed "to ensure all members of the public are treated equally", said the Home Office.
"Now let me be clear: I know the vast majority of officers police impartially and that policing without fear or favour is their creed," she will say.
But Mahmood will announce "clear, comprehensive guidance" on police impartiality, which reinforces that officers must apply the law consistently to avoid what she called "motivated actors" whipping up the idea that there's two-tier policing.
Mahmood will say that community engagement can mean going to a residents' association meeting and having tea and biscuits - or samosas - but it shouldn't mean engaging with activists pushing an agenda.
"Leave the politics to the politicians," she will say. "And we will leave the policing to you."
The home secretary will add that more needs to be done to tackle inequalities in policing, highlighting the persistently low proportion of black police officers.
However, she will state that some "well-intentioned approaches", such as the Police Anti-Racism Commitment, "have risked undermining confidence in impartial policing".
"As a Muslim home secretary, no one can doubt that equality in policing, and in our forces, matters to me," she will say.
"But we must also be wary of misguided attempts at course correction, where the pursuit of equality leads instead to differential treatment.
"To the public, it was patently absurd to tell police officers that fair policing "does not mean treating everyone the same".
Jo Noakes who leads the College of Policing, the standards-setting body for the police, said it will issue new guidance for officers that will make clear on impartiality in Spring.
She said: "Policing must act in a way that maintains public confidence, which is dependent on officers and staff exercising their powers without fear or favour...
"Impartiality cannot be seen in isolation but needs to be considered alongside how policing acts with fairness and inclusion - both in its own ranks and with the public."

title: Government risks missing climate targets if EV rules weakened, adviser warns
summary: The UK could miss legally binding climate targets if EV targets are cut, an adviser warns
body:
Current rules say all new cars must be zero emission by 2035
The UK is likely to miss legally binding climate targets if the government reduces electric vehicle (EV) targets, independent adviser the Climate Change Committee (CCC) has warned.
In a letter to Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander, the CCC argues that weakening the targets would result in "economic and energy security costs" and leave households "more exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices".
The CCC says that switching to an electric vehicle can save a typical household around £800 a year, with fewer people benefiting if the targets were watered down.
The warning comes afterweeks of speculationthat the government plans to announce changes to the EV targets. Government sources insist no decision has been made.
Under the current rules, a "zero emission vehicle" (ZEV) mandate requires 80% of new cars sold in the UK to be zero emission by 2030 and all new cars to meet that standard by 2035. Companies that fail to meet their ZEV mandate face a potential fine of £12,000 per car, although there are exemptions.
Industry groups have long complained the current rules impose too heavy a burden, calling instead for a "sustainable transition".
Latest data from trade body the Society of Motor Manufacturing and Traders (SMMT) shows that EVs, as well as plug-in hybrids, are driving growth in new car sales.
In the year so far, 26.6% of all new car registrations have been fully electric, the SMMT says, which is below the headline target of 33% for 2026.
But the industry as a whole appears on course to comply with this year's mandate once flexibilities are accounted for, according to analysis by New AutoMotive, a transport research organisation which supports the transition to electric cars
SMMT Chief Executive Mike Hawes accused the CCC of ignoring the costs of the targets it was defending.
"The industry cannot subsidise the transition indefinitely, which is why it is unified in seeking change," he said.
The CCC analysis also argued that weakening the targets would lead to a hole in the government's carbon savings that need to be made in order to meet its legally binding climate targets.
The CCC said the ZEV mandate "underpins the largest share of emissions reduction to 2037" in the government's net-zero plan.  The climate targets set for 2033-2037 will be missed "without alternative action at the same scale", the CCC argued.
CCC analysis shows surface transport - which includes cars, vans and trucks - remains the country's highest carbon-emitting sector and one of the slowest to decarbonise.
Lord Deben, former CCC chairman, said going against CCC advice would "not be sensible" as it would "cost people money".
He said climate targets were "not random targets" and "if you don't reach them then you put yourselves in really serious danger of having climate change, which we can't handle".
A government spokesperson said: "We remain committed to the phase out of all new petrol and diesel cars by 2030 and to all new car and van sales being zero emission by 2035, as well as to our legally binding net zero targets. Our consultation on the Mandate will not change this and will ensure we are taking a pragmatic and balanced approach to the ZEV transition."

title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
summary: It marks the first sanctions since the UK announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
body:
The E1 area east of Jerusalem is a strategically important part of the occupied West Bank
The UK has sanctioned companies it said are involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank.
The construction of settlements, which are illegal under international law, has risen sharply in recent years. Settler attacks on Palestinians and their property have also surged.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies".
Criticising the move on X, he wrote that Israel - as it has done in the past - will respond with "countermeasures", and that "decisions will be announced in due course".
"Israel will not bow to external pressure or change its policies as a result," Saar said, adding that they will "consider new ways to strengthen Jewish communities" in the West Bank, and "protect those involved in developing and building".
Israel previously condemned UK sanctions related to West Bank settlements, accusing the Labour government of "systematically acting against the State of Israel".
The Palestinian foreign ministry welcomed the sanctions and called on other countries to follow suit.
It comes two days before the deadline for bids for construction tenders in the highly sensitive E1 area east of Jerusalem.
The plans, which have been condemned internationally, would in effect divide the West Bank in two and cut it off from East Jerusalem.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said the E1 development would render a two-state solution "unviable" by "cutting through the heart of Palestine".
The sanctions also target Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement which the UK government says has organised and carried out blockades to prevent aid entering Gaza.
Responding to the announcement, the group said: "Tzav 9 is a movement of abiding citizens from all the political spectrum, and we've always protested peacefully."
It comes after the UK expanded its human rights sanctions regime last month, enabling the government to sanction individuals and companies involved in violations of international humanitarian law anywhere in the world.
The government is also developing separate legislation to ban the import of goods from Israeli settlementsand the provision of advertising services for settlement properties in the UK.
Miliband said: "Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this government's approach.
"That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution.
"The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable.
"We are committed to working productively with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to advance lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike."
In September, the UK government announced that it would ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements, as well as acting against companies and individuals providing services for settlement expansion.
At the time, Miliband said the move marked the beginning of a "new approach" to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, which "not only calls out injustice and suffering, but acts".
That announcementprompted a furious reaction from Israel, which said it would shut the British consulate in East Jerusalem in retaliation.
Last month, most diplomats left the consulate - which handled UK relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem as well as in the West Bank and Gaza -but the UK insisted that the building would not be closingand would operate as a "UK mission".
